title: SA/90/2007 of BALAM SINGH Vs SMT. PURNA DEVI

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 90 of 2007
Balam Singh .....Appellant
Versus
Smt. Purna Devi ....Respondent
Present :
Mr. Narayan Singh Negi, Advocate for the appellant.
Mr. V.K. Kaparwan, Advocate for the respondent.

Dated: 20th November, 2018
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.

This is a plaintiff's Second Appeal, wherein, he has
challenged the judgment and decree rendered by Civil Judge (Senior
Division) Uttarkashi, Purola in Civil Suit No. 01 of 2000, Balam
Singh Vs. Smt. Purna Devi, whereby, the Trial Court had dismissed
the suit by judgment dated 14.11.2002, which on a challenge being
given by the plaintiff appellant in regular Appeal under Section 96 of
the Code of Civil Procedure, by way of C.A. No. 12 of 2002, Balam
Singh Smt. Purna Devi has been affirmed and Appeal of the present
appellant to the Second Appeal has been dismissed on 24.04.2007.
Thus, the plaintiff challenges the concurrent judgment of both the
Courts below. This Court, while admitting the appeal has framed the
following substantial questions of law, which this Court has to
answer:
"Whether the courts below have erred in law in ignoring
the final decree, passed on 14.07.1987 in respect of Khasra
No.80 in case No.84/86-87, arising out of case No. 40/83-84
under Section 176 of U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land
Reforms Act, 1950 ? If so, its effect ? "
Besides this, no other substantial question of law has been pressed by
the appellant.

2
2. The land, in dispute, over which a decree of permanent
injunction was sought for, have been more particularly described in
the proceedings before the Court below, as having bandobasti khasra
No. 80, having an area of 0.013 hectares, situated in Village Sada,
Tehsil Badkot, District Uttarakashi. The plaintiff, appellant, herein,
to the Second Appeal, has filed a suit for decree of permanent
injunction on 02.02.2000, in relation to the property, in dispute, as
described in the plaint. In the suit, in question, he had come up with
the case that when efforts were being made by the defendant /
respondent for interfering over the property, in question, in 1999, it
was without an authority and title rested in her because the plaintiff
claimed to have got the property in exchange in a proceeding
concluded under Section 161 of U.P. Z.A. & L.R. Act, in his favour
which was decided by way of Revenue Case No. 75/1997-98, by the
judgment dated 31st August, 1998, this judgment had attained finality.
The argument of the learned counsel for the appellant is that in lieu of
his holding, he has exchanged the holding lying in khasra No. 80,
having an area of 0.013 hectares, as such, he has all the rights to
protect his possession from a wrongful interference in contravention
to the judgment and decree dated 31st August, 1998, as rendered in
Revenue Case No. 75/1997-98, Balam Singh and another Vs. Vishan
Singh, in a proceeding held under Section 161 of the Act.
3. The suit was contested by the defendant, who filed his
written statement on 07.04.2000 and in the written statement, more
particularly, in para 9 of the written statement, it had specifically
pleaded by defendant that no benefit would accrue to the plaintiff on
the basis of a decree of exchange under Section 161 of the Zamindari
Abolition and Land Reforms Act, as the same was a collusive decree
procured in collusion with Champa Devi. It was also submitted in the
written statement that the determination of rights between the parties
to the suit in a proceeding under Section 229-B, initiated at the behest
of the plaintiff by way of Suit No. 82 of 1989-90, Balam Singh Vs.
Birendra Lal and another already stood dismissed by the judgment of

3
the Assistant Collector on 19th December, 1989 which, subsequently
was affirmed by the Commissioner as well as by the Board of
Revenue. Thus, by virtue of this pleading, it is quite apparent that
when appellant has instituted proceedings under Section 229-B, which
happens to be the principal proceedings for declaration of title,
meaning thereby, according to him also, there was cloud over his title
and ownership over the property, in dispute, it was because of that the
appellant had to file a declaratory suit for perfecting his title, which
admittedly, stood affirmed upto the second Appellate Court, i.e. Board
of Revenue and has attained finality as not challenged further before
superior court by the appellant to the Second Appeal. Hence, the
argument of the learned counsel for the appellant before the Court
below as well as before this Court is that no suit for injunction could
have been entertained when the plaintiff / appellant, herein, has been
concurrently held by all the Courts below not to be the owner in
possession of the property, in question.
4. Another relevant aspect which is to be considered is that
the judgment and decree as rendered on 19th December, 1989 in a suit
for declaration under Section 229-B filed by the appellant, herein,
who is the plaintiff in the injunction suit, has not been put to
challenge, it would be taken that his suit would not satisfy the
parameters of Section 38 and 39 of the Specific Reliefs Act.
5. The defendant had submitted that defendant is widow of
Sabal Chand. She submitted that the property, in dispute, stood
partitioned about 65 to 66 years ago and based on family partition,
claimed property stood settled with her and is in cultivatory
possession and recorded in the revenue records jointly with other co-tenure holders. Defendant further submitted that there had been an
earlier proceedings under Section 161 registered before Assistant
Collector as Case No. 40 of 1983-84, in which, preliminary decree of
partition was made on 06.05.1986, but, no final decree could be
passed and no kuras were settled nor the same is recorded.

4
6. Before the learned Trial Court, there was another
argument raised to the effect that the defendant, respondent, herein, to
the suit of injunction filed by the appellant, had also filed a suit for
declaration under Section 229-B, being Suit No. 87 of 1995-96,
though, it was although dismissed by the Assistant Collector and
appeal against the said order is pending consideration before the
Commissioner.
7. On exchange of pleadings, the learned Trial Court framed
the following issues :

8. The plaintiff / appellant's sole basis of defending his
possession in a suit for injunction has been the proceedings under
Section 161 of the Act, i.e. Revenue Case No. 75 of 1997-98 as
decided on 31.08.1998. This Court is of the view that once there was
a prior decree of dismissal of his suit under Section 229-B, which
happens to be the regular statutory proceedings for declaration of
one's right and title over the property lying in revenue village, which
was preferred by the plaintiff himself and dismissed upto Board of
Revenue, in that eventuality, no proceedings of exchange held at a
later stage, which more or less is based on a consensus of exchange, in
relation to the same subject matter, in which, any right is said to have
been settled by way of exchange could be a valid settlement of rights
because the exchange of a land under Section 161 of the Act could
only be made with the land which is bonafidely held by the plaintiff in
accordance with law and there is a statutory right vested in the party
to the proceedings of exchange under Section 161 of Zamindari
Abolition Act.

5
9. Learned Trial Court, while considering the proceedings
before the Revenue Court held that the plaintiff has failed to make out
his case for the grant of decree of injunction and dismissed the suit.
The Appellant Court, too, had dismissed the appeal by the judgment
dated 24th April, 2007. The Appellate Court, too, has recorded the
concurrent finding of facts.
10. The appeal when it was admitted on 27th July, 2007, the
same has been admitted on the following substantial question of law :-
"Whether the courts below have erred in law in ignoring
the final decree, assed on 14.07.1987 in respect of Khasra No.
80 in Case No. 84/86-87, arising out of case No.40/83-84 under
Section 176 of U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms
Act, 1950 ? If so, its effect ?"
11. The issue by way of substantial question which has been
framed for determination pertaining to the non determination of the
effect of the partition decree said to have been rendered in Revenue
Case No. 40/83-84, under Section 176 of the Z.A. & L.R. Act on
06.05.1986, it may not hold for us for a longer period. The reason
being, admittedly, as per case of parties to the suit, after the
preparation of the preliminary decree, no final decree was prepared
and no kurabandi has been held and that is why, as a matter of fact,
the decree of partition never finalized nor made effective in absence
of final decree. The Trial Court, while considering the impact of the
decree rendered in Case No. 40/83-84 under Section 176 of the Act,
had compared the impact of the decree along with impact of the
decree rendered under Section 229-B, which are proceedings for
declaration of right drawn at later stage to the proceedings drawn by
the appellant, herein, in Case No. 82 of 1989-90, which too, stood
dismissed by the order dated 9th December, 1989 and affirmed upto by
the Board of Revenue by the judgment dated 11th June, 1996.

6
12. The substantial question, as sought to be considered, will
not arise as it is not the foundation of pleading by the plaintiff in a suit
for injunction nor it is the case of the plaintiff of divesting of any
settled right vested on him based on the so called decree for partition
rendered in Case No. 84 of 1986-87 allegedly decided by way of
preliminary decree dated 14.07.1987, which would otherwise has no
reference in the absence of preparation of final decree and settlement
of kuras. The question is decided against plaintiff as he does not
plead to protect his possession of property based on any settlement of
decree rendered in the partition suit.
13. While, dealing with the argument of the learned counsel
for the appellant regarding effect of judgement of exchange under
Section 161 of the Z.A. & L.R. Act though it is not a substantial
question of law, on which, the appeal has been admitted and this
Court would be required to answer the question but since it is being
pressed by the learned counsel for the appellant, it becomes necessary
for the Court to deal with the said issue.
14. It has been the consistent argument of the appellant, on
which, the appellant has harped upon is the effect of the decree of the
proceedings under Section 161, as rendered in Revenue Case No. 75
of 1997-98. On 31.08.1998, he submits that as a matter of fact on the
culmination of the proceedings under Section 161, the land in his
possession has exchanged hands, hence, he would have a right to
defend his possession over the land which has been exchanged by the
judgment dated 31st August, 1998 in Revenue Case No. 75 of 1997-
98.
15. This Court is not in agreement with the arguments as
extended by the learned counsel for the appellant for the reasons that :
1. His suit for declaration of his title under Section 229B
of the Zamindari Abolition Act already stood

7
dismissed upto the Board of Revenue by the judgment
dated 11th June, 1996, which has attained finality.
2. Once, his title stood denied by the competent regular
Revenue Court, there could not have been any
subsequent proceedings under Section 161 for the
same piece of land which was drawn at a later stage in
the year 1997.
3. Once the title was not settled of land in dispute due to
the dismissal of under Section 229-B of the appellant,
he could not have validly exchanged the property in
the proceedings under Section 161.
16. Hence, for the purposes of decree of injunction, at least
the judgment dated 31st August, 1998 under Section 161 of the Act
cannot be attracted for getting a decree on the basis of the parameters
under Sections 38 and 29 of the Specific Relief Act. Thus, this Court
is of the view that the substantial question of law, as sought to be
pressed by the appellant, is not involved in the present Second
Appeal. Hence, same is answered in negative against the appellant.
Hence, the Second Appeal is dismissed.
17. However, there would be no order as to costs.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 20.11.2018
